The Proximal Operator of a Separable Penalty, by Its Stationary Points

Source: R/prox.R
dot-prox_root.Rd

Returns, for every coordinate, the stationary point of smallest objective \((\beta - v_j)^2/(2t) - \log f(\beta)\), where \(f\) is the parent's density, among the stationary points found on the segment between \(v_j\) and the mode of the parent. When the parent is unimodal, this point is the global minimizer. The function serves the separable penalties that have no closed-form operator, such as the heavy-tailed Student t prior.

Usage

.prox_root(penalty, v, step, theta, n_grid = 64L)

.prox_mode(ly)

.prox_root_widened(penalty, h, vi, m = 0)

.prox_uniroot(h, lo, hi, flo, fhi)

Arguments

penalty

A DistribPenalty() object with no map and a block width of one.

v

A numeric vector, the points towards which the operator pulls.

step

The step length \(t\), a single positive finite number.

theta

The aligned hyperparameter list.

n_grid

The number of grid points on each segment, including both ends.

ly

The function \(\ell^{(y)}\) of the parent, vectorized.

h

The function \(h\) of one coordinate.

vi

That coordinate's point.

m

The parent's mode, as .prox_mode() returns it.

lo, hi

The ends of a bracket, in either order.

flo, fhi

The values of h there, of opposite signs.

Value

A numeric vector of the same length as v.

.prox_mode() returns a single number, the mode of the parent or zero.

Details

The stationary points are the roots of \(h(\beta) = (\beta - v)/t - \ell^{(y)}(\beta)\), whose second term is distributions7::distrib_grad_y(). For a density that is not log-concave \(h\) can have more than one root (up to three for the Student t, two of them local minima of the objective), and the first root that a bracket encloses need not be the global minimizer.

For a unimodal parent with mode \(m\), the penalty is non-increasing up to \(m\) and non-decreasing after it, so the global minimizer lies on the segment between \(v\) and \(m\). Moving a point beyond \(v\) to \(v\), or a point beyond \(m\) to \(m\), lowers the quadratic term and does not raise the penalty. The mode is the root of \(\ell^{(y)}\), found once per call because the parent and \(\theta\) are the same for every coordinate: when \(\ell^{(y)}(0)\) is exactly zero the mode is taken as zero, and otherwise the root is bracketed by doubling a step from zero in the direction in which \(\ell^{(y)}\) points, up to \(2^{60}\), and refined by uniroot() to full relative precision. When the search finds no change of sign, or \(\ell^{(y)}\) is not finite, the mode is taken as zero and the segment is the one between zero and \(v\). The search moves away from zero only while \(\ell^{(y)}\) keeps its sign, so the root that it finds is a local mode, which is the mode when the parent is unimodal.

The function scans the segment on n_grid equally spaced points that include both ends, and evaluates \(h\) for every coordinate in one call. It refines by uniroot() every interval over which \(h\) changes sign, keeps as it is a grid point where \(h\) is exactly zero, and returns the candidate of smallest objective, computing the log-density with distributions7::distrib_pdf().

When the segment shows no change of sign, the bracket starts one unit beyond \(\min(v, m)\) and \(\max(v, m)\), each end that does not yet have the required sign is moved out by the current width of the bracket up to sixty times, and the single root found in the final bracket is returned. For a parent with more than one mode, the result in either case is a stationary point that need not be the global minimizer, because the scan covers only the segment between \(v\) and one local mode.

The tolerance passed to uniroot() is eps^0.75 times the end of the bracket nearer to zero, or the smallest positive double when the bracket has zero as an end or contains it. uniroot() adds 2 eps times the current iterate to that tolerance, so the root is found to a relative accuracy whatever its magnitude.

Errors

The message names the penalty where the stationary condition changes sign neither on the segment nor in the widened bracket.
